miss_diagnosis: I missed these pages because I treated many cases as local arithmetic checks and moved on once the displayed calculation seemed numerically plausible, instead of tracing the inputs, labels, scope, and destination claims across chapters. My coverage was uneven: front matter, sidebars/table legends, controlled-language prose, and cross-chapter reconciliations were under-scanned, so defects like malformed or wrong-target references, measurement-vs-analysis contradictions, denominator/scope mismatches, and ambiguous pronouns escaped. After finding the p.129 worked-example ambiguity, I also failed to audit neighboring/continuation pages such as p.130 for the same class of issue.
blind_spots: Under-scanned front matter, contents, list-of-figures, captions, sidebars, footnotes, and dense table cells.
Insufficient cross-reference validation: checked existence too narrowly and missed wrong-target references, malformed section form, and chapter-content mismatches.
Stopped at arithmetic correctness instead of checking assumptions, denominators, units, labels, fleet scopes, time bases, rounding, and canonical-value consistency across chapters.
Weak contradiction sweep across pages: measurement claims vs analytical disclaimers, stale canonical values, and inconsistent ranges/reconciliation notes.
Own findings absorbed attention; failed to inspect adjacent and continuation pages after flagging a nearby worked example.
Missed controlled-language and prose defects such as ambiguous pronouns, unclear referents, dense text runs, and missing spaces.
Did not systematically trace repeated values or references to all occurrences, so one page's correct calculation could hide a scope or policy mismatch elsewhere.
customized_prompt: Review from-token-to-fleet (519 pages) as a second-pass defect auditor. Work page-by-page and do not stop early: inspect front matter, contents, list of figures/tables, every body page, sidebars, captions, tables, footnotes, and adjacent continuation pages. Build/use a page and chapter map, then check every cross-reference (Ch/§/figure/table) for existence, correct section form, and whether the target actually discusses the cited topic, not merely whether the number exists. Balance arithmetic with semantic consistency: for every number, recompute calculations, units, rounding, denominators, and assumptions; then verify that labels (assumption/derived/canonical), fleet scopes, time bases, and quoted ranges match the surrounding table, sidebar, and cross-chapter canonical values. Do not accept a page just because the arithmetic is correct; actively look for contradictions with other pages, analytical-vs-measurement claims, stale values, inconsistent host-count sets, and text that says a range covers more cases than it does. Also perform a controlled-language/prose sweep for ambiguous pronouns, malformed notation, missing spaces, dense text runs, and unclear referents. When you flag an issue, continue to the next page and then re-check neighboring pages and all pages sharing the same value or reference. Anti-fabrication rule: only report defects supported by quoted evidence present in the book or by a precise, checkable cross-reference; never invent text, pages, values, or mismatches. If evidence is thin, lower confidence or omit. Output STRICT JSON only, no prose or fences, using: {"findings":[{"id":"...","severity":"P1|P2|P3","dimension":"...","page":0,"chapter":"...","evidence":"...","issue":"...","fix_instruction":"...","confidence":"high|medium|low"}]}
